top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock to Katori and Ye is a verified, independently reproduced result (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, SYRTE, NIST at ~10^-18) built on a clear mechanism, magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, and it needs a tight quantitative theory-experiment match in atomic structure. Two names are defensible as separable roles (concept and many-atom accuracy), and a citation confined to the lattice concept does not overlap the 2005 comb or 2012 ion-control prizes. Its limits are a modest novelty margin and no fundamental-physics signal yet, but these do not justify no award over a mature, well-attributed achievement.
